examples.en: My grandfather farmed all his life.
She lived with books her whole life.
In my whole life, I have never had food this good.
He donated the money he had saved over a lifetime to a school.

examples.ko: 저는 일평생 이 동네를 떠난 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never left this town in my entire life.

examples.ko: 일평생 후회하지 않을 선택을 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to make a choice I will never regret in my life.

explain: '평생'과 거의 같지만 '일평생'은 좀 더 힘주어 말하거나 글에서 쓰는 느낌이 있어요. 대화에서는 '평생'이 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요. 보통 '일평생 ~만 하다'처럼 부사처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '평생', but '일평생' sounds a bit more emphatic or written. In conversation '평생' is often more natural. It is usually used like an adverb, as in '일평생 ~만 하다'.

examples.en: I packed some reading material for the train.
This magazine has a lot of interesting things to read.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 가벼운 읽을거리가 필요해요.
examples.en: I need something light to read when I travel.
There was nothing to read in the hospital waiting room.

examples.ko: 아이에게 읽을거리 좀 사 주려고 해요.
examples.en: I am going to buy my child something to read.
Let me tell you about a website with plenty to read.

explain: 책, 잡지, 기사처럼 읽을 수 있는 것을 두루 가리켜서 '책'보다 가볍게 들려요. '읽을거리가 많다/없다', '읽을거리를 챙기다'처럼 자주 써요. '볼거리', '먹을거리'와 짝으로 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It covers anything you can read, such as books, magazines and articles, so it sounds lighter than '책'. Common patterns are '읽을거리가 많다/없다' and '읽을거리를 챙기다'. It is easy to remember together with '볼거리' and '먹을거리'.

examples.en: After the greasy food, I cleansed my palate with tea.
Do you want some cold fruit to freshen your mouth?
I rinse my mouth with water before brushing.
Let's have the dongchimi later to clear our palate.

examples.ko: 고기를 먹은 뒤에 냉면으로 입가심하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people finish a meat meal with cold noodles.
I will chew a piece of gum to freshen my mouth.

explain: 보통 '입가심하다'로 쓰고, '입가심으로', '입가심 삼아'가 자주 나와요. 물로 입안을 헹굴 때도 쓰고, 식사 뒤에 차나 과일, 냉면으로 입맛을 정리할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '입가심하다', and '입가심으로' and '입가심 삼아' are very common. You can use it for rinsing your mouth with water, or for finishing a meal with tea, fruit or cold noodles to reset your taste.

examples.ko: 입금자 이름이 달라서 확인이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The depositor's name is different, so I can't confirm it.
Do you know who the depositor is?

examples.ko: 입금자명에 주문하신 분 이름을 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please write the name of the person who ordered in the depositor name field.
I will send the item after I check who paid.
Yesterday some money came in from an unknown sender.
It is fine if the payer and the orderer are different.

explain: 온라인 쇼핑에서 '입금자명'이라는 말로 가장 많이 만나요. 돈을 받는 쪽은 '수취인'이라고 해요. 통장에 찍히는 이름이 주문자 이름과 같으면 확인이 쉬워요.
explain_en: You will meet it most often as '입금자명' (depositor name) in online shopping. The person who receives the money is the '수취인'. Confirmation is easier when the name shown on the bank record matches the orderer's name.

examples.ko: 큰 개는 밖에서 입마개를 해야 해요.
examples.en: Large dogs have to wear a muzzle outside.
My puppy hates the muzzle, so it is hard.

examples.ko: 입마개 사이즈가 너무 작은 것 같아요.
examples.en: The muzzle seems too small.
Be sure to bring a muzzle when you go for a walk.
Thanks to the muzzle, we avoided a biting accident.

examples.ko: 새 입마개는 숨쉬기 편해서 개가 잘 써요.
examples.en: The new muzzle lets the dog breathe easily, so he wears it well.

explain: 일상에서는 주로 개에게 씌우는 입마개를 말해요. 사람이 쓰는 건 '마스크'라고 해서 서로 달라요. '입마개를 하다/씌우다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In daily life it mostly means the muzzle put on a dog. What people wear is a '마스크', so the two are different. Use it as '입마개를 하다/씌우다'.

examples.en: I must have been tired, because I got mouth sores.

examples.ko: 입병 때문에 매운 음식을 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: I can't eat spicy food because of my mouth sores.
I bought some medicine that is good for mouth sores.

examples.ko: 요즘 입병이 자꾸 생겨서 병원에 갈까 해요.
examples.en: Mouth sores keep appearing lately, so I'm thinking of seeing a doctor.
When you have mouth sores, even eating is hard.
I have often had mouth sores since I was little.

explain: 보통 '입병이 나다/생기다'로 말하고, 피곤할 때 입안이나 입술이 헐거나 부르트는 것에 자주 써요. '입안이 헐다'도 비슷하게 말해요.
explain_en: It is usually said as '입병이 나다/생기다' and is often used when your mouth or lips get sore after being tired. '입안이 헐다' is a similar way to say it.

examples.ko: 둘이 또 사소한 일로 입씨름을 해요.
examples.en: Those two are bickering again over something small.

examples.ko: 입씨름 좀 그만하고 이제 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Stop arguing and let's eat now.
If I argue with my brother, I lose anyway.

examples.ko: 입씨름 끝에 결국 제가 먼저 사과했어요.
examples.en: After the squabble, I ended up apologizing first.
As the meeting dragged on, it was nothing but wrangling.
It is better to avoid pointless arguments.

explain: 몸싸움이 아니라 말로만 티격태격하는 걸 말하고, 결론 없이 계속 따지는 느낌이 있어요. '말다툼'보다 가볍게 쓸 때가 많아요. '입씨름을 하다/벌이다'로 써요.
explain_en: It means a fight with words only, not fists, and it often feels like going back and forth with no conclusion. It is often a bit lighter than '말다툼'. Say '입씨름을 하다/벌이다'.

examples.ko: 이 보험은 입원비뿐 아니라 간병비도 보장해요.
examples.en: This insurance covers not only hospital fees but also caregiver costs.
The hospital bill came out higher than I expected.
You pay the hospital fees all at once when you are discharged.
I struggled to raise the money for my father's hospital stay.
I have to send the hospital fee receipt to the insurance company.
Hospital fees and medicine costs together add up to quite a lot.

explain: '병원비'는 병원에서 드는 돈 전체이고, 입원비는 병원에 입원해 있는 동안 드는 돈이에요. 보험 이야기에서 '입원비 지원/보장'으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '병원비' covers all money spent at a hospital, while '입원비' is the cost of staying in the hospital as an inpatient. It often appears in insurance talk, as in '입원비 지원/보장'.

examples.en: There were a lot of visitors at the amusement park today.

examples.ko: 입장객은 모두 손목에 도장을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: All entrants have to get a stamp on their wrist.
The number of museum visitors rose compared with last year.
They give free water bottles to people who enter.
Because of the rain, the number of visitors was cut in half.
The visitors are lining up and waiting.

explain: 공연장, 박물관, 경기장처럼 어딘가에 들어온 사람을 셀 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '입장객 수'로 자주 나와요. '관람객'은 보러 온 사람이라는 점이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when counting people who entered a venue such as a concert hall, museum or stadium. In the news it often appears as '입장객 수'. '관람객' puts more focus on people who came to watch something.

examples.en: I burned the roof of my mouth on hot pizza.
The roof of my mouth is scraped and it hurts.
Touch your tongue to the roof of your mouth.
A peanut skin is stuck to the roof of my mouth.
The skin on my palate peeled off, so I can't eat anything.
At the dentist they even checked the roof of my mouth carefully.

explain: '입천장을 데다', '입천장이 까지다/벗겨지다'처럼 뜨거운 음식을 먹고 다쳤을 때 특히 자주 써요. 의학에서는 '구개'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used most often when you hurt it on hot food, as in '입천장을 데다' or '입천장이 까지다/벗겨지다'. The medical term is '구개'.

en: start of spring (Ipchun, a solar term)

examples.en: Ipchun has passed, but it is still cold.

examples.ko: 입춘에 대문에 글귀를 붙이는 집도 있어요.
examples.en: Some households put up a written phrase on the gate on Ipchun.
This year Ipchun is in early February.
A late cold snap often comes around Ipchun.
Maybe because it is Ipchun, the sunlight feels different.
They say spring starts from Ipchun, but it still feels like winter.

explain: 달력으로는 봄이 시작되는 날이지만 날씨는 아직 추울 때가 많아서, '입춘이 지났는데도 춥네요' 같은 말을 자주 해요. 이날 '입춘대길'이라는 글귀를 붙이는 풍습도 있어요.
explain_en: On the calendar it marks the start of spring, but the weather is often still cold, so people say things like '입춘이 지났는데도 춥네요'. There is also a custom of putting up the phrase '입춘대길' on this day.

examples.en: You can deposit and withdraw freely with this account.
I checked my transaction history in the app.

examples.ko: 입출금 통장을 하나 새로 만들고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to open a new checking account.

examples.ko: 입출금 수수료가 무료인 은행을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a bank with no deposit or withdrawal fees.

examples.ko: 은행 점검 시간에는 입출금이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Deposits and withdrawals aren't possible during the bank's maintenance time.
Deposit and withdrawal alert texts keep coming.

explain: 은행에서 '입출금 통장'이라는 말로 가장 많이 만나요. 돈을 넣는 것이 '입금', 빼는 것이 '출금'이고, 둘을 합친 말이에요. ATM이나 앱 화면에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You will meet it most often in '입출금 통장' (an everyday account) at a bank. Putting money in is '입금' and taking it out is '출금', and this word combines them. It also appears often on ATM and app screens.

examples.en: My parents are a well-known loving couple in the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 두 분은 잉꼬부부처럼 늘 손을 잡고 다니세요.
examples.en: They always walk hand in hand like a devoted couple.
I heard they are a devoted couple married for over forty years.
An actor famous as half of a loving couple appeared.
I also want to live as a loving couple someday.
They are supposed to be a devoted couple, but I hear they had a big fight yesterday.

explain: 사이가 아주 좋은 부부를 말해요. 보통 남이 칭찬할 때 '잉꼬부부 같으세요'처럼 쓰고, 자기 부부를 말하면 자랑처럼 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a couple who get along very well. People usually use it to compliment others, as in '잉꼬부부 같으세요', and using it about yourself may sound like bragging.

en: financial difficulty; stringency of capital; lack of funds

examples.en: The company closed because of a shortage of funds.
I heard the shop is having cash trouble.
Many small businesses suffer from a lack of funds.
The construction stopped halfway due to a funding shortage.
To solve the cash shortage, they borrowed money from a bank.
The funding crunch got so bad that even employees' pay was delayed.

explain: 회사나 가게 같은 곳의 운영 돈이 모자랄 때 써요. 개인 이야기라면 '돈이 없다', '쪼들리다'가 더 자연스러워요. '취업난', '구인난'처럼 '-난'이 붙은 말과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used when a company or shop runs short of operating money. For an individual, '돈이 없다' or '쪼들리다' sounds more natural. It helps to learn it with other '-난' words such as '취업난' and '구인난'.

examples.ko: 이 운동은 자기만족을 위해 하는 거예요.
examples.en: I do this exercise for my own satisfaction.
Even if no one notices, I get a lot of personal satisfaction.
It's just for my own satisfaction.
If you get stuck in self-satisfaction, it is hard to improve.
What I started for my own enjoyment became my job.

examples.ko: 이 봉사는 제 자기만족인 것 같기도 해요.
examples.en: I sometimes think this volunteering is just for my own satisfaction.

explain: 좋은 뜻으로는 '내가 좋아서 하는 일'이고, 나쁜 뜻으로는 남은 별로인데 혼자 만족한다는 느낌이에요. '자기만족을 위해'는 보통 편하게 쓰고, '자기만족에 빠지다'는 부정적이에요.
explain_en: In a good sense it means doing something because you enjoy it, and in a bad sense it means being satisfied alone while others are not impressed. '자기만족을 위해' is usually neutral, while '자기만족에 빠지다' is negative.

examples.ko: 반복 업무를 자동화하면 시간이 많이 절약돼요.
examples.en: If you automate repetitive tasks, you save a lot of time.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 포장 과정을 모두 자동화했어요.
examples.en: This factory has automated the whole packaging process.
Banks are increasingly automating counter work.
I tried automating report writing with Excel.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 자동화하려다 오히려 더 복잡해졌어요.
examples.en: I tried to automate everything and it got more complicated instead.

examples.ko: 업무를 자동화한 뒤 처리 속도가 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: After we automated the work, processing got faster.

explain: 사람이 하던 일을 기계나 프로그램이 하게 만들 때 써요. '업무를 자동화하다'처럼 목적어와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 앱이나 기계가 스스로 하는 건 '자동으로 ~하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when you make a machine or program do work that people used to do. It is often used with an object, as in '업무를 자동화하다'. For things an app or machine does by itself, you can also say '자동으로 ~하다'.

examples.ko: 그는 키가 큰 것을 자랑삼아 말해요.
examples.en: He talks about being tall as something to brag about.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 신발을 자랑삼아 친구에게 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The child showed his new shoes to a friend as a boast.

examples.ko: 오래 다닌 회사를 자랑삼는 사람은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many people take pride in a company they have worked at for long.

examples.ko: 친구는 새 차를 자랑삼아 온 동네를 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: My friend drives around the whole town to show off his new car.
My hobby isn't something I'd boast about.
Don't brag about something like that.

explain: '~을 자랑삼아 ~하다'처럼 쓰는 경우가 대부분이에요. '자랑하다'는 그냥 뽐내는 것이고, '자랑삼다'는 어떤 것을 자랑거리로 내세우는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the pattern '~을 자랑삼아 ~하다'. '자랑하다' simply means to show off, while '자랑삼다' feels like holding something up as your thing to be proud of.

examples.en: The child proudly held out the drawing.
He proudly held up his certificate.
Grandmother talked proudly about her grandson.
My daughter greeted me with a proud smile.

examples.ko: 새 가방을 자랑스레 메고 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: She went to school proudly carrying her new bag.
The players waved the flag proudly.

explain: '자랑스럽게'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 주로 글이나 이야기에서 동작을 꾸밀 때 쓰고, 말할 때는 '자랑스럽게'가 더 흔할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '자랑스럽게'. It is mostly used in writing or storytelling to describe an action, while '자랑스럽게' may be more common in speech.

examples.en: I couldn't get up even when the alarm clock rang.

examples.ko: 내일 아침 여섯 시에 자명종을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I set the alarm clock for six o'clock tomorrow morning.
I was startled by the sound of the alarm clock.
I turned off the alarm clock and fell back asleep.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 자명종은 소리가 아주 커요.
examples.en: The alarm clock at Grandpa's house is very loud.
It seems the alarm clock battery has run out.

explain: 요즘은 휴대폰의 '알람'을 더 많이 쓰고, '자명종'은 알람이 달린 탁상시계를 말할 때가 많아요. '자명종을 맞추다/끄다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: These days people use the phone '알람' more, and '자명종' often refers to a desk clock with an alarm. Say '자명종을 맞추다/끄다'.

examples.en: I saw a charity pot on the street at year-end.
I put a thousand won into the charity pot.

examples.ko: 자선냄비 종소리가 들리면 겨울이 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: When I hear the charity pot bell, it feels like winter has come.
Our company took part in the charity pot fundraiser.
The children stopped in front of the charity pot.
I heard this year's charity pot donations went up from last year.

explain: 구세군이 연말에 거리에 세우는 모금 냄비를 주로 말해요. 종소리와 함께 겨울을 알리는 모습이라 연말 분위기와 같이 떠올리는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to the donation pots the Salvation Army sets up on streets at year-end. With the ringing bell, many people associate it with the year-end atmosphere.

examples.en: I studied alone using a study guide.
I bought one math study guide.
This study guide has easy explanations.
Read the study guide before the workbook.
All the answers are in the study guide.
Thanks to the study guide, I finished my homework quickly.

explain: 교과서 내용을 풀어서 설명해 주는 책이에요. 문제를 많이 푸는 '문제집'과는 달라요. 혼자 공부할 때 설명을 보려고 찾는 책이라고 생각하면 돼요.
explain_en: It is a book that explains textbook content. It is different from a '문제집', which is for solving lots of problems. Think of it as the book you look at for explanations when studying alone.

en: asking for it; bringing something upon oneself

examples.ko: 숙제를 안 했으니 혼나는 건 자업자득이에요.
examples.en: You didn't do your homework, so getting scolded is your own fault.
I can only say he brought it on himself.
Being late because you woke up late is your own doing.
It is my own doing, so who can I blame?
I know it's my own fault, but I'm still upset.
It is a situation where the word 'self-inflicted' fits perfectly.

explain: 자기가 한 행동 때문에 나쁜 결과를 받았을 때 써요. 남에게 직접 말하면 차갑게 들릴 수 있어서, 보통 자기 이야기를 하거나 뒤에서 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used when someone suffers a bad result because of their own actions. Saying it directly to someone can sound cold, so it is mostly used about yourself or when talking about others behind their back.

examples.en: Water flowing downward is also a law of nature.
Scientists study the laws of nature.
No one can change the laws of nature.
This experiment proceeds according to the laws of nature.
That is as natural as a law of nature.

examples.ko: 자연법칙 덕분에 비행기가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the laws of nature, airplanes can fly.

explain: 중력처럼 늘 똑같이 작용하는 규칙을 말해서, 사람이 정하는 '법'이나 '규칙'과는 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 '당연한 이치'라는 뜻으로 비유해서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to rules like gravity that always work the same way, so it differs from '법' or '규칙' made by people. In daily talk it is also used figuratively to mean something that is only natural.

en: being wild; being taken from nature

examples.en: This raw fish restaurant sells only wild fish.
Wild pine mushrooms are expensive.
Is this fish farmed or wild?

examples.ko: 자연산이라서 맛이 더 좋은 것 같아요.
examples.en: Because it is wild, it seems to taste better.
I tried wild sea bream for the first time.
There is a big price difference between wild and farmed.

explain: 반대말은 물고기라면 '양식', 채소나 버섯이라면 '재배'예요. 식당에서 생선, 버섯, 나물을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '양식' for fish, and '재배' for vegetables or mushrooms. It is often used at restaurants when talking about fish, mushrooms and wild greens.

examples.en: The answer to this problem has to be a natural number.
Adding natural numbers always gives a natural number.

examples.ko: x에 들어갈 수 있는 자연수를 구하세요.
examples.en: Find the natural numbers that can go in x.
I'm confused about whether 0 counts as a natural number.

examples.ko: 계산해 보니 자연수가 아니라 소수로 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I calculated, it came out as a decimal, not a natural number.
What is the smallest natural number?

explain: 수학 시간에 '정수', '소수'와 함께 자주 나와요. 한국 학교 수학에서는 보통 0을 자연수에 넣지 않고 1부터 시작해요.
explain_en: It often appears in math class along with '정수' and '소수'. In Korean school math, 0 is usually not counted as a natural number and the count starts from 1.

examples.en: My self-control weakens in front of sweet food.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 자제력을 잃으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you are angry, you must not lose your self-control.

examples.ko: 야식을 참다니 정말 자제력 있는 분이네요.
examples.en: You resisted a late-night snack, so you really have self-control.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 자제력을 기르는 연습이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need to practice building self-control from childhood.
Self-control doesn't develop overnight.
At the last moment I held back my words through self-control.

explain: 하고 싶은 것이나 화를 스스로 멈추는 힘을 말해요. '참을성'은 힘든 것을 견디는 쪽이고, 자제력은 해 버리고 싶은 것을 스스로 멈추는 쪽에 가까워요. '자제력을 잃다/기르다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the power to stop yourself from doing what you want or from getting angry. '참을성' leans toward enduring hardship, while '자제력' leans toward stopping yourself from acting on an urge. Common patterns are '자제력을 잃다/기르다'.

examples.en: The evening sky turned purplish.
The dark purple skirt suits you well.
The grapes have ripened and have a purplish tint.
My mother gave me a dark purple scarf as a gift.
The tips of the petals have a purplish color.
My arm turned purple from a bruise.

explain: '보라색'보다 붉은 기가 도는 짙은 색이에요. 일상에서는 '보라색'이 더 흔하고, 자줏빛은 묘사하는 글에서 자주 나와요. 표기는 '자주빛'이 아니라 '자줏빛'이에요.
explain_en: It is a deep purple with a reddish tint, compared with '보라색'. In daily talk '보라색' is more common, and '자줏빛' shows up more in descriptive writing. The spelling is '자줏빛', not '자주빛'.

examples.en: The school prepared the event on its own.
The company started its own internal investigation.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 팀 안에서 자체적으로 해결할게요.
examples.en: We'll solve this problem within the team.
We have our own standards, so we inspect separately.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 자체적으로 쓰레기를 줄이고 있어요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood is reducing waste on its own.
I'll check the cause on our own.

explain: 밖의 도움 없이 그 안에서 스스로 한다는 뜻으로, 보통 '자체적으로'로 써요. '자체 조사', '자체 제작'처럼 '자체'만 붙이는 말도 많아요.
explain_en: It means doing something from within, without outside help, and is usually used as '자체적으로'. Many phrases just use '자체', such as '자체 조사' and '자체 제작'.

examples.en: The children draw pictures on the ground with a stick.
Grandfather walks leaning on a stick.
I picked fruit using just one stick.

examples.ko: 텐트를 작대기 몇 개로 받쳐 놓았어요.
examples.en: I propped up the tent with a few poles.
The stick I picked up on the road is quite sturdy.
I tied a string to a stick and made a fishing rod.

explain: '막대기'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 군대에서는 계급장의 줄을 '작대기'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '막대기'. In the military, the stripes on a rank insignia are also called '작대기'.

examples.ko: 오늘 작업량이 너무 많아서 야근해야 해요.
examples.en: Today's workload is so big that I have to work overtime.
The team members split the workload among themselves.
There aren't enough people for the amount of work.
This week's workload is smaller than last week's.
I can't manage the workload, so it's hard.
The workload suddenly doubled.

explain: 사무 일에는 '업무량'을 쓰고, 작업량은 공장, 공사, 편집처럼 직접 손으로 하는 작업에 더 잘 어울려요. '작업량이 많다/적다', '작업량을 줄이다'로 써요.
explain_en: For office work people use '업무량', and '작업량' fits hands-on jobs such as factory work, construction and editing better. Say '작업량이 많다/적다' and '작업량을 줄이다'.

examples.ko: 큰따옴표 안의 말을 다시 인용할 때는 작은따옴표를 써요.
examples.en: Use single quotation marks when you quote something inside double quotes.
Inner thoughts are marked with single quotation marks.
The single quotation marks are missing, so the sentence feels awkward.
I emphasized this word by putting it in single quotation marks.
The single quote key is next to Enter on the keyboard.
Newspaper headlines often use single quotation marks.

explain: 큰따옴표는 직접 대화나 인용에 쓰고, 작은따옴표는 속마음, 강조, 인용 안의 인용에 써요. 신문 제목에서는 말을 줄여서 인용할 때도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Double quotation marks are for direct speech or quotes, while single ones are for inner thoughts, emphasis and quotes within quotes. Newspaper headlines also often use them to quote shortened remarks.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 흥행은 못 했지만 작품성은 높아요.
examples.en: This film wasn't a box office hit, but its artistic quality is high.
It won a big award for its artistic merit.

examples.ko: 저는 작품성보다 재미를 먼저 따지는 편이에요.
examples.en: I tend to care about fun before artistic quality.
Critics rated it as having outstanding artistic quality.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 작품성과 인기를 모두 잡았어요.
examples.en: This drama gained both artistic quality and popularity.
Please recommend a novel with artistic value.

explain: 영화, 소설, 그림 같은 작품을 예술적으로 얼마나 잘 만들었는지 말할 때 써요. '흥행성', '대중성'과 비교하며 '작품성은 좋은데 인기는 없다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used to talk about how well a film, novel or painting is made as art. It is often compared with '흥행성' and '대중성', as in '작품성은 좋은데 인기는 없다'.

examples.en: I seem to be coming down with a cold, since I have a slight cough.
A little cough keeps me from sleeping well every night.
He came into the room with a small cough.
Even a light cough, if it continues, should be checked at a hospital.
I keep hearing small coughs from the next seat.
The light cough lasted a long time, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 크게 콜록거리는 기침이 아니라 작고 자주 나오는 기침이에요. '헛기침'은 목을 가다듬거나 신호로 일부러 하는 기침이고, 잔기침은 자꾸 나오는 작은 기침에 주로 써요.
explain_en: It is a small, frequent cough rather than a big hacking one. '헛기침' is a cough you make on purpose to clear your throat or give a signal, while '잔기침' mostly refers to small coughs that keep coming.

examples.en: My mom is a notorious nagger.
My ears hurt because of my nagging older sister.
That teacher is a nagger, so students avoid her.
I don't want to become a nagger.
My husband teases me by calling me a nag.

examples.ko: 잔소리꾼도 다 나를 생각해서 그러는 거죠.
examples.en: Even naggers do it because they care about me.

explain: 가족이나 친한 사이에서 농담 반으로 많이 써요. 면전에서 말하면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요. '장사꾼', '일꾼'처럼 '-꾼'이 붙은 말과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is often used half jokingly among family or close friends. Saying it to someone's face can offend them. It helps to learn it with other '-꾼' words such as '장사꾼' and '일꾼'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 가게에서 잔심부름을 했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I ran small errands at a local shop.
New employees start by learning the small errands.

examples.ko: 잔심부름 좀 해 주면 용돈 줄게요.
examples.en: If you run a few small errands for me, I'll give you pocket money.
I was worn out by little errands all day.

examples.ko: 잔심부름이 많아서 정작 제 일은 못 했어요.
examples.en: There were so many odd errands that I couldn't do my own work.
As the youngest, the small office errands are my job.

explain: 우편물 부치기, 커피 사 오기처럼 작고 번거로운 일에 써요. 보통 '잔심부름을 하다/시키다'로 말해요. '잔소리', '잔주름'처럼 '잔'이 붙으면 작고 자질구레하다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for small, bothersome tasks such as mailing things or buying coffee. It is usually said as '잔심부름을 하다/시키다'. As in '잔소리' and '잔주름', the prefix '잔' gives a feeling of small and minor.

examples.en: Fine lines form around my eyes every time I smile.
With makeup, fine wrinkles are less visible.

examples.ko: 화면이 너무 선명해서 얼굴의 잔주름까지 다 보여요.
examples.en: The screen is so sharp that even fine wrinkles on the face show.
I look older because of the fine lines.
Fine wrinkles have increased on the backs of my hands too.
I heard this cream is good for caring for fine lines.

explain: 눈가나 입가에 생기는 가늘고 작은 주름이에요. 깊게 패인 건 그냥 '주름'이라고 해요. '주름살'도 비슷하게 쓰고, '잔주름이 생기다/늘다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: These are thin, small wrinkles around the eyes or mouth. Deep ones are just called '주름'. '주름살' is used similarly, and you say '잔주름이 생기다/늘다'.

examples.en: Today is a party day at our house.
On the feast day, people from the whole village gathered.
I set out lots of delicious food like it was a party day.
Grandmother's birthday was our family's party day.
The house was busy from the morning of the party day.
It's raining on the party day, so I'm worried.

explain: 결혼식, 돌, 환갑처럼 잔치를 하는 날이에요. '오늘 완전 잔칫날이네'처럼 기쁜 일이 겹치는 날에 비유로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the day of a celebration such as a wedding, a first birthday or a 60th birthday. It can also be used figuratively, as in '오늘 완전 잔칫날이네', when happy things come together.
